entities.summary: Dmitry Ivanovich Donskoy was a medieval Russian prince who played a pivotal role in the politics and culture of 14th-century Russia. He was the grandson of Ivan Kalita and the son of Ivan II, and he succeeded his father as Grand Prince of Vladimir in 1363. Donskoy was a key figure in the struggle for Moscow's dominance over the other Russian principalities, and he played a crucial role in the formation of the Grand Duchy of Moscow. His reign was marked by a series of military campaigns against the Tatars, the Mongols, and the Lithuanians, which ultimately led to the defeat of the Golden Horde and the establishment of Moscow as the dominant power in Russia. Donskoy was also a patron of the arts and architecture, and his court was renowned for its cultural achievements. He died on May 27, 1389, and was buried in the Vladimir-Suzdal Cathedral in Vladimir, Russia. Donskoy's legacy continued to shape Russian history, and he remained a revered figure in Russian folklore and literature for centuries.
